summary: Frontend E2E testing of Fase 3 'Álbum AI' (/album) completed successfully. All 6 requested behaviors validated end-to-end using the authenticated session cookie and the 10 JPGs from /app/test_photos. Empty state renders on load; folder-input accepts the test_photos directory; 10 photos are laid out into spreads (Portada + 4 spreads at Balanced density); density switching correctly changes spread count (Airy=8, Balanced=5, Dense=4); the cover toggle flips checkbox state; 'Ordenar con IA' successfully calls /api/ai/album-order and renders a coherent Spanish rationale in album-ai-reason (~15s); 'Exportar PDF' triggers a browser download of Album_test_photos.pdf with zero console errors during the entire flow.

issues: Cover template renders as a half-white / half-image spread. With the solid-color test JPGs this looks visually asymmetric; likely intentional (photo on right page, blank left page) but worth confirming with real wedding photos.

critical_code_review_comments: AlbumStudio.jsx uses webkitdirectory input; for automated tests, note that Playwright requires a directory path (not file list) when set_input_files targets a webkitdirectory input. Not a bug, but documenting for future testing agents.
No console errors emitted during the full flow (upload -> plan -> density switching -> AI order -> PDF export). Good hygiene.

context_for_next_testing_agent: To test /album with Playwright, set the session_token cookie first, then call page.set_input_files('[data-testid=album-folder-input]', '/app/test_photos') passing the DIRECTORY PATH (not a file list) because the input has webkitdirectory. Wait for [data-testid=album-spreads] (up to 45s). AI order call takes ~10-20s and reveals [data-testid=album-ai-reason]. Export PDF uses jsPDF doc.save; capture with page.expect_download(). Baseline spread counts on 10 test photos: airy=8, balanced=5, dense=4.
